------------------------------------------------------------ FINAL REPORT - CT CHEST ABDOMEN PELVIS WITH CONTRAST AND BONE SCINTIGRAPHY Name: Wojciechowski, Tadeusz Exam date: 6/3/2086 Referring: Dr. Vasudeven Dictated by: Ingrid Solheim-Baptiste, MD. Dictated but not read. Transcribed 06/04/2086.
CLINICAL HISTORY: Eighty-nine year old gentleman with known prostate carcinoma, diagnosed March of this year, restaging. Prior CABG, ischemic heart disease, CKD, diabetis.
TECHNIQUE: Axial images were obtained from the thoracic inlet through the symphysis pubis following the administration of intravenous contrast, adjusted for the patients reduced eGFR. Whole body planar and SPECT images were obtained three hours following injection of technetium.
FINDINGS: The prostate gland is enlarged and heterogenous with extension into the left seminal vesicle. There are multiple pelvic lymph nodes the largest measuring 1.4 cm in short axis in the left obterator chain. In the skeleton there are several foci of increased uptake, within the lumbar spine at L3 and L4, the right ileum and the left proximal femur, in keeping with osseous metastatic disease. The lungs are clear apart from some linear scaring at the bases which is old. Status post sternotomy with intact wires and coronary bypass graft clips.
IMPRESSION: 1. Locally advanced prostate carcinoma with pelvic nodal and multifocal osseous metastasis. 2. No visceral metastasis. Recomend correlation with PSA and tissue sampling per Oncology.
